chapter: Later ventures, lodges and San Francisco recollections
title: Taking the bootblack chair to New York, 1938-40
summary: Spikes took Richard's hydraulic bootblack chair to New York to lease it, with hundreds sold before the war killed the project.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: Oh, I think in...when I took that bootblack chair back there. See? That's about '38 or '39. Y'see, my brother invented it, and what we were gonna do is to lease it, not sell 'em, you see, 'cause we could build them for about twenty-five dollars, and a motor you could get for six or seven dollars--that was one of the biggest things--and we was gonna let 'em rent out at twenty per cent, and you know, those days, every parking lot had a bootblack stand on it, see? And I took it back all...I got big pictures of it in there somewhere...all the way back

to New York, where the...uh, and I had about four...five hundred of them sold, but then the war come and couldn't get no material--couldn't get any motors, couldn't get no steel, you couldn't get nothin'... That just blowed it up. We never did get back into it any more. I got big pictures of me here on it somewhere, back in New York. Oh... I don't know where that stuff is. Cut it off.
